title: Object-ball throw versus cut angle
purpose: Validates the 1/7 sticking constant and the Coulomb cap on the tangential impulse. Also records a known model limitation (see known_deviations).
sources: Alciatore, 'The Amazing World of Billiards Physics' (2007), TP A-14 throw data

params.note: object ball placed along the cut-angle bisector per row

known_deviations: The model caps the tangential impulse at mu_ball*J_n, which gives a constant throw angle of atan(mu_ball) = 2.86 deg once the balls start slipping (cut angles above ~18.8 deg). The measured throw is speed dependent and larger on slow shots (up to 5.5 deg at a 40 deg cut) because the table's static friction during the collision raises the effective friction. This is the correction described by Kim 2024 and is not implemented.
In the sticking regime (cut angles below ~18.8 deg) the model predicts atan(2*tan(cut)/(7*(1+e))), which gives 1.48 deg at a 10 deg cut against a measured 1.45 deg - agreement to 0.03 deg.
